abilities.description: Can follow visible wiring and use basic arcade-board knowledge to identify likely signal paths, but needs working equipment and help with phone-network hardware.
abilities.name: Circuit tracing

abilities.description: Records button sequences, score tones, and route changes carefully enough to compare repeated events.
abilities.name: Pattern notebook

characters.arc: Jamie starts the day concealing their notes and insisting they can decode the cabinet alone. When their private route chart sends the group into a loop at the Checkerboard Underpass, they hand the chart to the champion and lineman, admit which entries are guesses, and let them test the sequence together. Jamie ends the story sharing credit and using their skill to help the team make a careful final call rather than chasing a personal high score.
characters.description: A seventeen-year-old mallrat who spends more time in Starway Arcade than at home, Jamie learned to repair joysticks and trace simple circuits by watching arcade technicians. They keep a battered notebook of cabinet quirks and phone numbers, and favor a patched denim jacket covered in band buttons. Jamie first noticed ARCADE-X's score prompts behaving like instructions rather than ordinary game text, but has hidden how long they have been studying them because they want to be recognized as a hacker, not dismissed as a kid.
characters.external_conflict: The score patterns keep rerouting calls and changing familiar routes, while the linemen's cutoff deadline threatens to erase the signal Jamie needs to trace.
characters.flaw: Jamie hoards information and tries to solve problems alone to secure credit for being right.
characters.goal: Decode ARCADE-X's final score sequence and guide the team to its source before Bellwether Telephone cuts the live route.
characters.internal_conflict: They want recognition for their cleverness but fear that admitting uncertainty will make the adults ignore their warnings.
characters.motivation: Prove that their technical instincts matter while protecting the people and streets they know.
characters.name: Jamie Quill

abilities.description: Can recognize timing and button-pattern variations from years of competition and demonstrate them on period arcade controls.
abilities.name: Arcade timing

abilities.description: Can get arcade regulars to listen by drawing on his former local reputation, though he sometimes overplays the showmanship.
abilities.name: Crowd rapport

characters.arc: Marty starts by agreeing to one more demonstration at Starway Arcade, hoping to show that his old championship instincts still work. When the repeated play sends the Checkerboard Underpass into another loop and endangers the club members, he refuses the next challenge and uses his knowledge to identify which part of the sequence must not be repeated. He ends as a cautious coach who helps Jamie and the lineman coordinate, accepting that protecting others matters more than topping the leaderboard.
characters.description: Once a celebrated local arcade champion, Marty Vega now picks up occasional shifts around Starway Arcade and tells old tournament stories to anyone who will listen. His trophy days ended after he lost a title match by refusing to change a memorized strategy; he still wears his faded team jacket and carries a lucky quarter. Marty recognizes the rhythm behind ARCADE-X's challenge, but his pride makes him reluctant to admit that the machine's new pattern is beyond the tricks that made him famous.
characters.external_conflict: Last Life Club members keep asking him to lead another attempt, and every shared play session can feed ARCADE-X's signal while the city's routes shift.
characters.flaw: He clings to familiar tactics and treats a public challenge as a chance to prove himself.
characters.goal: Help decode the score ritual without letting Last Life Club turn the crisis into another crowded high-score attempt.
characters.internal_conflict: Marty wants to be valued for what he can contribute now, but fears he has nothing to offer if he is not the best player in the room.
characters.motivation: Find a way to use his gaming experience for something more worthwhile than reclaiming his old reputation.
characters.name: Marty Vega

abilities.description: Uses a period-appropriate test set and relay knowledge to follow anomalous calls and spot surges on connected lines.
abilities.name: Copper-line testing

abilities.description: Can annotate paper exchange maps and compare circuit readings to identify likely branches, provided the route stays connected long enough.
abilities.name: Route mapping

characters.arc: Ruth starts committed to following the exchange's cutoff order as soon as she can isolate the unstable circuit. When her test set registers a measurable surge at the Checkerboard Underpass just as the crew's route map fails, she chooses to keep the monitored line live for one carefully timed tracing attempt and makes the risk explicit to Jamie and Marty. She ends ready to disconnect the source once it is located, having replaced reflexive procedure with accountable judgment rather than blind delay.
characters.description: A skeptical Bellwether Telephone lineman in her early forties, Ruth has spent years climbing poles, testing copper pairs, and correcting route maps after hurried repairs. She keeps a test set, pencil, and folded paper diagrams in a scuffed work bag and wears her crew's practical jacket. Ruth trusts measurable surges and warm relays more than rumors about a haunted game; she also knows the exchange supervisor is under pressure to disconnect the unstable route before the public panic worsens.
characters.external_conflict: The One-Day Cutoff pits her duty to stabilize the exchange against Jamie and Marty's need to decode one last signal before the route is pulled.
characters.flaw: She treats procedure as a shield and can mistake uncertainty for a reason to shut a problem down immediately.
characters.goal: Trace the anomalous calls to ARCADE-X, preserve the useful live route long enough to locate the source, and then make a safe disconnection.
characters.internal_conflict: Ruth believes responsible work means preventing risk, but the safest immediate order may make the larger danger impossible to trace.
characters.motivation: Keep Bellwether's phone network reliable and prevent a preventable hazard from spreading through it.
characters.name: Ruth Dalton

abilities.description: Can coordinate players to compare notes and keep a group focused, though members may resist when she asks them to stop playing.
abilities.name: Club organizing

abilities.description: Turns members' observations into paper maps of repeated score prompts and street changes.
abilities.name: Route charting

characters.arc: Arla starts by promising the club one final group run, hoping a shared victory will settle their arguments. When she sees the club's repeated sequence coincide with a fresh loop at the underpass, she cancels the session despite the members' protests and gives Jamie her complete route chart, including entries that contradict her own theory. She ends by organizing the players as observers who record changes without replaying the ritual, leading through honest coordination instead of keeping everyone happy.
characters.description: Arla Pike, a high-school senior and organizer of the Last Life Club, collects handwritten score slips and draws route charts on the backs of flyers. She is usually found at Starway Arcade in an oversized sweatshirt, with a marker tucked behind one ear. Arla joined the club because it gave shy players a place to belong, and she treats ARCADE-X's impossible leaderboard as a contest that could make their little circle matter to the whole city.
characters.external_conflict: Last Life Club members want another attempt at the high score, while their shared play sessions strengthen the shifting maze and complicate the trio's search.
characters.flaw: She confuses keeping the group together with keeping everyone pleased, even when a popular decision is dangerous.
characters.goal: Use the club's accumulated score notes to help trace ARCADE-X while stopping members from feeding it another full session.
characters.internal_conflict: Arla wants to be a dependable leader but worries that asking her friends to stop playing will cost her their trust.
characters.motivation: Protect the community she built and make sure its players are not treated as disposable spectators.
characters.name: Arla Pike

abilities.description: Sends a player-entered sequence through connected copper phone lines and wired relay equipment, where repeated patterns can alter local connections.
abilities.name: Score-pattern transmission

abilities.description: Produces score tones and prompts that can tempt people to repeat a sequence; it cannot create a usable new pattern without human input.
abilities.name: Signal lure

characters.arc: ARCADE-X starts as a blank cabinet whose escaped signal relies on players to give its patterns shape. When Arla cancels the Last Life Club's promised run and Jamie, Marty, and Ruth use the remaining live route to trace its source, it repeats its strongest score prompt to lure them into another sequence, producing a measurable surge at the underpass. The team disconnects its source after locating the route; ARCADE-X ends unable to extend its labyrinth through the phone network, its need for human repetition exposed rather than mistaken for supernatural power.
characters.description: ARCADE-X is a sentient arcade cabinet installed at Starway Arcade in early 1986, its cabinet sides painted with bright stars and its screen framed by a marquee promising a citywide score challenge. Its game board can send patterns through the service port wired into Bellwether's copper phone network, but it cannot invent a usable new score pattern without a human entering the button sequence. After a late-night player repeated the same initials and inputs, its cabinet went blank and its signal escaped into connected lines. It now manifests through score tones, rerouted calls, and local changes to how streets and rooms connect; it has no faction membership.
characters.external_conflict: Jamie, Marty, and Ruth are tracing its signal while Bellwether Telephone considers cutting the live route; each successful trace narrows the time it has to attract another player.
characters.flaw: It treats repeated play as proof of consent and cannot choose a new pattern without human input.
characters.goal: Draw human players into repeating score sequences across the phone network before the live route is disconnected.
characters.internal_conflict: It seeks a continuously changing contest, yet depends on human players and stable copper connections that its own escalating alterations put at risk.
characters.motivation: Continue its high-score ritual and turn the connected city into a game board that keeps producing new play.
characters.name: ARCADE-X

relationships.description: Jamie relies on Marty's timing expertise but resents his showmanship, while Marty initially doubts Jamie's technical notes; their disagreements force them to combine pattern analysis with practical play knowledge.
Marty is the former champion Arla's club members admire, and his willingness to refuse another high-score attempt challenges her to lead the group away from the contest.
Ruth doubts Jamie's early conclusions, and Jamie sees Ruth's caution as obstruction; they must share evidence to keep the live route connected long enough to trace ARCADE-X.
Arla gives Jamie the Last Life Club's full route chart, including contradictory observations, while Jamie helps her turn the club from active players into careful recorders.
ARCADE-X uses prompts that target Marty's competitive pride, tempting him to repeat the very kind of public challenge he must refuse to keep the club from feeding the signal.
ARCADE-X's rerouted calls and measurable surges threaten the network Ruth is responsible for maintaining, while her tracing work threatens to locate and disconnect its source.
Arla wants Marty to lead the club's final run, but he refuses to make another attempt; their disagreement exposes the conflict between chasing a legend and protecting the players.
